subject: Can I implement this joint-likelihood model in r-INLA?

messages.author: d07cf6c199aec725
messages.subject: Can I implement this joint-likelihood model in r-INLA?
parts:
Hi,

Can I specify the following BUGS/JAGS model in r-INLA? 

model {
   
    for (j in 1:nsite){
    z[j] ~ dbin(psi[j],1)
    muy[j] <- z[j]*p
    Y[j] ~ dbin(muy[j],5)

    lambda[j] <- z[j]*exp(alpha1)
    muP[j] <- E[j]*lambda[j]
    W[j] ~ dpois(muP[j])
   }    
}

If possible, do I just need to specify separate distributions (e.g., family = c(rep("Binomial",2), "Poisson") and the `Z` will be carried across or is there some additional step that I need to do?


Thanks for your time,
Brent

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Can I implement this joint-likelihood model in r-INLA?
parts:
Hi

you're asking about two zeroinflated observation, where the 'inflated'
process is the same. As you have written it now,
it cannot be done, as there might be a zero form 'dbin' and 'dpois'
with z[j] = 1. If you have the version that if Y[j] = 0, then z[j] =1,
(type 0, versions) so there is this separation, then this is possible.
I'm not sure if this simplification is of any use

Best
H
